subject: China orders AI firms to reject US capital
body_text:

April 24th, 2026 · 8 alerts worth your attention
Alerts feature Preview.
You're getting this because you subscribe to AI Weekly. The stories below went out this morning to readers who opted into our breaking alerts. If you want them in your inbox going forward, there's a one-click opt-in at the bottom.
China orders AI firms including ByteDance and Moonshot AI to reject US capital without state approval
Bloomberg · 2026-04-24
Chinese regulators have instructed tech firms including ByteDance, Moonshot AI, and StepFun to reject US-origin capital without explicit government approval, Bloomberg reports. The directive is a direct response to Meta's $2B acquisition of Chinese-founded AI startup Manus and aims to prevent further loss of AI assets to American buyers. Several affected startups are now unwinding offshore corporate structures ahead of domestic IPOs.
Read →
Musk reveals Tesla Terafab will use Intel's 14A process for AI chips, making Intel's first major foundry customer
The Register · 2026-04-23
Elon Musk announced Tesla will use Intel's next-generation 14A process node to manufacture AI chips at its planned Terafab complex in Austin, Texas. The deal makes Tesla Intel's first major 14A foundry customer — a breakthrough for Intel's struggling contract manufacturing business — while SpaceX, xAI, and Tesla plan two fabs targeting vehicle autonomy and AI data center workloads.
Read →
40,000 Samsung workers rally demanding AI chip profit share, threaten 18-day strike next month
Washington Post · 2026-04-23
About 40,000 Samsung Electronics workers rallied at the company's Pyeongtaek chip complex demanding the bonus cap be scrapped and 15% of operating profit shared with workers. The union is threatening an 18-day strike next month, which could further strain global AI memory chip supply already tight from surging HBM demand.
Read →
DeepSeek releases V4 open-source flagship: 1.6T-param MoE with 1M context under Apache 2.0
Hugging Face · 2026-04-24
DeepSeek released V4-Pro (1.6T parameters) and V4-Flash (284B parameters) on April 24 with 1M-token context windows under Apache 2.0. The open-source models claim best-in-class agentic coding among open-weight models and quality approaching Claude Opus 4.6 non-thinking mode. Multiple HN front-page submissions totaling 500+ points.
Read →
Tencent and Alibaba in talks to invest in DeepSeek at $20B+ valuation, doubling earlier target
The Information · 2026-04-23
Tencent and Alibaba are in talks to join DeepSeek's first external funding round at a valuation above $20 billion, doubling the $10B+ target reported days earlier. Tencent has proposed acquiring up to a 20% stake, though DeepSeek is resisting ceding that much control.
Read →
SpaceX IPO filing reveals plans for in-house GPU manufacturing to support AI ambitions
Taipei Times (Reuters) · 2026-04-24
SpaceX disclosed in its $1.75T IPO filing that it plans to manufacture its own GPUs, listing in-house chip production among 'substantial capital expenditures.' The company warned investors it lacks long-term contracts with direct chip suppliers, and the effort is linked to the Terafab joint venture with Tesla, xAI, and Intel.
Read →
OpenAI officially releases GPT-5.5 'Spud' with 2x pricing and new agentic capabilities
TechCrunch · 2026-04-23
OpenAI released GPT-5.5, codenamed 'Spud,' on April 23 to paid ChatGPT and Codex subscribers, just six weeks after GPT-5.4. The model scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 73.1% on Expert-SWE, with API pricing doubling to $5/$30 per million input/output tokens and a 1M context window.
Read →
Meta installing software to record employee keystrokes and mouse movements to train AI agents
CNBC · 2026-04-22
Meta's 'Model Capability Initiative' records US employees' clicks, keystrokes, and screenshots across work apps to train AI agents that can perform white-collar tasks autonomously. Multiple employees called the program 'dystopian' in internal messages, citing concerns about sensitive data exposure.
